units.translation: For their ungovernable minds carry them to defeat.
overcome by desire, where it is constructed with the genitive, as in Choephori 1052: 'do not be overcome by fear.' For thus Porson rightly corrected for 'being conquered by fear.'
overcome by sleep.
overcome by gains.
overcome by words.
not overcome by sleep.
For the blessed, even being defeated is fitting.
Let us know whether we are winning or being defeated.
For you have not been defeated.
I may be defeated
I am defeated
victory
victory.
Yet even a shameful victory the god honors.
May victory, since it has followed, remain steadfast.
Do you also honor this victory of the contest?
Send aid to the children eagerly for victory. Thus Portus for 'victory'.
May it be for victory.
Having unenviable pollutions of this victory.
Such things as are overseers of victory (Hermann: of strife) not evil.
But to send what is profitable for the city's victory.
May victory and power be with the men.
victory-bringing
bringing victory.
With the gods and Earth and Justice who brings victory.
Not having obtained a victory-bringing outcome.
A saving wrestling and victory-bringing of the spear.
him, her, it
See ἵ.
him, her, it
Niobe
was the title of a play of Aeschylus (fr. 154-164).
wash-water
wash-water.
And indeed it is necessary to bring wash-water for the feet of the god-bearers.
Nisus
Nisus, son of Pandion.
Having deprived Nisus of his immortal lock of hair.
snowstorm
snow falling in heaps.
And with white-winged snowstorm and earthly thunderings let him stir up everything.
Improperly fr. 196, 7: with a snowstorm of rounded stones he will make the ground shadowed.
When the roar of the destructive snowstorm falling is at the gates.
to snow
I snow.
of the destructive snowstorm falling, where 'falling' is read from the copies. In M 'snowing' with alpha written over eta, which is the older reading, about which see Thes. vol. 5 p. 1530.
nomads
nomads. Thus are called peoples not having a fixed abode, especially the Scythians: see Thes. vol. 5 p. 1540.
You will bring the Scythian nomads.
In the feminine gender Suppl. 284: I hear that the Indian nomads (thus rightly Bothius for 'Indians') ride on camels with saddles.
flock
flock.
The verb νομεύω [to pasture] is not infrequent, but νόμευμα [flock] is not read elsewhere.
With the rich flocks of sheep in their fine-wooled pasturings.
to pasture
flock
to hold as custom
I hold as custom.
I think, I consider.
Passive νομίζεσθαι [to be customary] is said of things that are established by custom.
Thinking life to be deprived of silver.
And someone formerly believing in no gods, i.e. believing that gods exist.
For we consider enmity in the house to be common.
You consider the inner chamber rich in wealth. The scholiast explains it by 'you drive' and 'you manage,' who may seem to have read something else.
For I consider the presence of the master to be the eye of the house.
You have from us such things as are customary.
Let them go having obtained by lot, as is customary. 423: where rejoicing is nowhere customary.
to be customary
lawful
lawful.
the laws. Sept. 334: before the lawful things.
custom
custom.
law.
